Each unit file /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-JuniorYearFlashcardsApp/56c5f561-7c60-57f9-af90-832dbd49ccc3/scratchpad/gen/out/lang-<unit>.json (units rhs, cle, reo, stl and x) has a "frq" list; the entries whose "kind" is "mc" are stimulus-based sets (a "stem" and "parts", each part with "l", "q" holding the question and its choice lines — "(A) …" or "A. …" — "a" the key followed by the explanation, and "n" a note). tellverify-a:
You are independently verifying "Tell apart" content for an AP study app: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-JuniorYearFlashcardsApp/56c5f561-7c60-57f9-af90-832dbd49ccc3/scratchpad/gen/out/tell-chem.json, /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-JuniorYearFlashcardsApp/56c5f561-7c60-57f9-af90-832dbd49ccc3/scratchpad/gen/out/tell-calcbc.json. Read /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-JuniorYearFlashcardsApp/56c5f561-7c60-57f9-af90-832dbd49ccc3/scratchpad/gen/SPEC-tell.md first. Each pair has two labels (a, b) and 6 to 8 statements, each keyed k = "a" or "b" with a reason "why". In the app, the student sees the two labels and one statement and taps the side it is true of.

For every statement: first decide yourself, without reading its k or why, which side it is true of. It must be true of exactly one side and false of the other; a statement that is true of both, of neither, or that a strong student could reasonably argue either way is a defect. Then compare with k, and check that the why is accurate. Verify every fact that is not textbook-standard with WebSearch, and recompute every number (python/sympy). For English Language, check the terms are used as the College Board CED uses them; for French, check every French sentence is correct and idiomatic (a fill-in-the-blank must have exactly one idiomatic answer: e.g. "il est l'heure" and "c'est l'heure" are both idiomatic, so such an item is a defect).

Fix defects in place: edit the statement so it becomes unambiguous, correct k or why, or delete the statement (a pair must keep at least 6 statements with at least 2 on each side; add a new correct statement if a deletion would break that). Edit the files directly with python, keeping their structure, and after each pair run `python3 /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-JuniorYearFlashcardsApp/56c5f561-7c60-57f9-af90-832dbd49ccc3/scratchpad/gen/tell_check.py <course>` (never with "merge") until it prints PASS. Do not write anything under /home/user/JuniorYearFlashcardsApp. Keep a log at /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-JuniorYearFlashcardsApp/56c5f561-7c60-57f9-af90-832dbd49ccc3/scratchpad/gen/out/audit-tellverify-a.md: one line per statement changed or deleted, with the reason. Save as you go, so an interruption loses little; if the log exists, continue from where it stops.

When you finish, reply with: statements checked per course, how many of your blind judgments matched k, each change in one line, and nothing else.
